title: T. rex: Clues from the King

theme.vibe: Fossil dig adventure with giant footprints

cover.title: T. rex: Clues from the King
cover.subtitle: A Real Dinosaur Mystery

pages.text: Meet T. rex! Its full name is Tyrannosaurus rex, which means tyrant lizard king. This giant dinosaur lived near the end of the Cretaceous Period.
extras: T. rex lived about 68 to 66 million years ago.

images.alt: A side-view life restoration of Tyrannosaurus rex walking on two legs

pages.text: T. rex was huge, but it was not a stiff tail-dragger. It held its body forward, balanced by a long, heavy tail.
extras: Many adults were about 12 meters long.
That is longer than a school bus.

images.alt: A scale chart comparing T. rex specimens with a human

pages.text: Powerful back legs carried T. rex across ancient North America. Its giant head reached forward, and its tail helped keep the whole animal steady.
extras: T. rex walked on two legs.

images.alt: An illustrated T. rex showing strong legs, a large head, and a balancing tail

pages.text: Open wide! T. rex had about 60 teeth. They were serrated like tiny saws, and its jaws could crunch bone.
extras: Some teeth were as long as a banana.

images.alt: A historic scientific diagram showing the skull and jaws of T. rex

pages.text: Was T. rex a hunter or a scavenger? Scientists think it could be both. Many meat-eaters hunt when they can and eat found food when they find it.
extras: A strong nose helped T. rex sniff out food.

images.alt: A life reconstruction of T. rex standing alert

pages.text: Those tiny arms are famous! Compared with the body, they were small. But they had strong muscles, and scientists still study what T. rex used them for.
extras: Small arms are a real dinosaur mystery.

images.alt: A T. rex life restoration showing its small arms and long tail

pages.text: We do not have a photograph of a living T. rex. We have fossils! Bones, teeth, bite marks, and growth rings help scientists build the story.
extras: Fossils are clues from deep time.

images.alt: A mounted T. rex fossil skeleton in a museum

pages.text: One famous T. rex is called SUE. SUE was found in South Dakota and is one of the largest and most complete T. rex skeletons ever discovered.
extras: SUE lived to about 28 years old.

images.alt: The T. rex skeleton SUE displayed at the Field Museum
